entries.title: Palliative Approach to Care (Definition and Enhanced Model)

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service; https://mcc.ca/objectives/medical-expert/dying-patients/, version March 2026)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Obj25 is scoped to the already-dying patient; this unit's broader framing -- that a palliative approach is 'not just for EOL' and may run concurrently with disease-modifying treatment from diagnosis onward (the 'enhanced model') -- is a real, testable timing concept (e.g., the Temel et al. early-palliative-care-referral paradigm cited in the chapter's own sidebar) that only partially overlaps obj25's dying-patient scope, so evidence strength is MODERATE rather than STRONG.

testable_competencies.timing: Recognize that a palliative approach can be initiated alongside curative/disease-modifying treatment early in a life-limiting illness, not only at the end of life.

entries.title: Palliative Care Assessment Tools (ESAS, Palliative Performance Scale)

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service; https://mcc.ca/objectives/medical-expert/dying-patients/, version March 2026)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Obj25's enabling objectives require symptom control and an appropriate management plan for the dying patient; ESAS (symptom-burden screening) and PPS (functional-status/prognostic scale) are the validated instruments used to operationalize that assessment, though neither tool is separately named in the objective text.

testable_competencies.tool_selection: Distinguish the purpose of the ESAS (patient-reported symptom-intensity screening across 9-10 domains) from the PPS (clinician-rated functional status with prognostic value, read by dropping down the ambulation column).

entries.title: Pain and Symptom Management (WHO Pain Ladder, Table of Common Symptoms)

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service; https://mcc.ca/objectives/medical-expert/dying-patients/, version March 2026)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Direct match: obj25's key objective explicitly requires the candidate to 'develop an appropriate goals-of-care plan that optimally controls pain and other symptoms' and its enabling objectives specify 'using pharmacologic and nonpharmacologic measures for symptom control (e.g., pain, respiratory distress, delirium, agitation) while recognizing appropriate indications, adverse effects, and possible complications' -- precisely this unit's WHO pain-ladder and symptom-management-table content.

testable_competencies.symptom_control: Select an appropriate first-line pharmacologic or non-pharmacologic approach for a common palliative symptom (pain, dyspnea, nausea/vomiting, constipation, delirium/agitation, secretions) using the WHO pain-ladder stepwise-escalation principle and general symptom-management categories.
testable_competencies.escalation_logic: Apply the WHO pain ladder's stepwise non-opioid to weak-opioid to strong-opioid escalation principle, distinguishing nociceptive from neuropathic and bony pain management categories.

entries.cross_discipline_note: The chapter's own in-text redirects send detailed opioid pharmacology to Anesthesia (A25: 'Pain Management') and Neurology (N43: 'Pain Syndromes'); this unit's scope is the palliative-context symptom-category framework and escalation principle rather than exhaustive drug-dose detail, consistent with the project instruction not to freeze changing opioid doses/conversion ratios/titration schedules at scope stage.

entries.title: Care of the Dying Patient (Predictors of Decline, Final Hours, Final-Days Care)

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service; https://mcc.ca/objectives/medical-expert/dying-patients/, version March 2026)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Direct match: this is the paradigm case of obj25's 'dying patient' scope -- recognizing the trajectory toward death (predictors of decline, changes in the last hours of life) and developing the final-days management plan (non-oral medication routes, discontinuing non-essential medications, planning for an expected death in the home) is exactly the recognize-and-act competency the objective describes.

testable_competencies.recognition: Recognize clinical predictors that a patient is entering the final months/hours of life (functional decline, comorbidity burden, sentinel events, Cheyne-Stokes breathing, terminal restlessness, mottling).
testable_competencies.management: Plan appropriate final-days care, including non-oral medication routes when swallowing is unsafe and discontinuing non-essential medications.

entries.title: Psychosocial and Spiritual Needs (incl. FICA Spiritual Assessment)

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service; https://mcc.ca/objectives/medical-expert/dying-patients/, version March 2026)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Obj25's enabling objectives require 'ensuring a culturally sensitive approach to emotional, physical, and spiritual supports for the patient and their family,' which frames this unit's psychosocial/spiritual assessment content, though the objective does not name a specific assessment framework such as FICA.

testable_competencies.assessment: Recognize the distinct psychosocial (psychological/emotional/social) vs. spiritual (meaning, value, purpose) domains of a holistic palliative assessment, and apply the FICA framework (Faith, Importance, Community, Address) to a spiritual-needs conversation.

entries.title: End-of-Life Decision Making (Advance Care Planning, Goals of Care, Code Status)

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service; https://mcc.ca/objectives/medical-expert/dying-patients/, version March 2026)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Direct match: obj25's enabling objectives require determining decision-making capacity, identifying an SDM when capacity is absent, and 'discussing with the patient or substitute decision-maker the patient's wishes for their care (e.g., full resuscitation) at the appropriate time' -- exactly this unit's Goals of Care and Code Status content.

testable_competencies.code_status: Distinguish full code, DNR/comfort measures, and Allow Natural Death (AND) terminology, and recognize that CPR is rarely effective and a DNR order is almost always consistent with palliative goals of care in advanced incurable illness.
testable_competencies.timing: Recognize the clinical triggers for initiating an EOL care discussion (recent hospitalization for serious illness, severe progressive disease, anticipated death within 6-12 mo, a MAID request).

entries.cross_discipline_note: The chapter explicitly redirects Power of Attorney for Personal Care mechanics to Ethical, Legal, and Organizational Medicine (ELOM15), and Ontario's default-SDM/capacity framework underlying this unit's Advance Care Planning content is the same legal machinery covered by ELOM's Consent and Capacity unit (MCC 121-1). This PM unit's scope is the clinical goals-of-care/code-status conversation and its timing in a palliative trajectory, not the underlying consent-capacity legal test itself, per the project instruction not to duplicate ELOM merely because a topic appears in an EOL context.

entries.title: Communication in Palliative Care (incl. SPIKES Protocol for Breaking Bad News)

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service; https://mcc.ca/objectives/medical-expert/dying-patients/, version March 2026)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Obj25 explicitly requires the candidate to 'know the provisions in Canadian law on MAID, be prepared to discuss them with patients' and to develop a goals-of-care plan through discussion with the patient/SDM -- both of which depend on the communication and bad-news-delivery skills this unit covers (SPIKES protocol, estimating and communicating life expectancy).

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service; https://mcc.ca/objectives/medical-expert/legal-ethical-and-organizational-aspects-of-medicine/truth-telling/, version February 2017)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: MCC's Truth Telling objective (121-2, Medical Expert, Ethics/Legal/Organizational Aspects group) explicitly names 'delivering bad news' as one of the challenging situations candidates must communicate accurately and effectively in -- the same general ethical/communication principle this unit applies concretely via the SPIKES mnemonic in a palliative context.

testable_competencies.bad_news: Apply the SPIKES protocol (Setting, Perception, Invitation, Knowledge, Emotions, Strategy/Summary) to structure a bad-news or prognosis-disclosure conversation.
testable_competencies.prognostication: Communicate prognosis using imprecise time-frame language (e.g., hours to days, weeks to months) rather than an overly specific estimate, recognizing that clinicians consistently overestimate survival.

entries.cross_discipline_note: ELOM's Truth Telling / Disclosure unit (MCC 121-2) is expected to carry the general ethical-legal principle of honest, accurate disclosure applicable across all of medicine. This PM unit is the discipline-specific application -- the SPIKES structured-interview protocol and prognosis-communication norms as taught in the palliative context -- and should be treated as a CROSS_DISCIPLINE link to that ELOM unit rather than a duplicate of it; PRIMARY_OWNER/CROSS_LINK/DISTINCT_CONTEXT designation is deferred to the global cross-chapter ownership audit per project instruction.

mcc_evidence.objective_title: Collaborator - Participate effectively on health care teams
mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (role-level record; no per-objective ID exists for this role)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Group's enabling text explicitly requires the candidate to 'explain the scope of practice and demonstrate respect for the expertise of each member of the team' and 'agree on and implement team members' responsibilities and roles' -- directly matching this unit's interprofessional-team-roster content (physicians, nurses, social workers, pharmacists, OT/PT, dieticians, spiritual care workers).

testable_competencies.team_roles: Identify the distinct roles of physicians, nurses, social workers/case managers, pharmacists, occupational/physical therapists, dieticians, and spiritual care workers on an interprofessional palliative care team.

entries.title: Suffering: Definition, Sources, and Relief of Refractory Physical/Existential Suffering

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service; https://mcc.ca/objectives/medical-expert/dying-patients/, version March 2026)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Direct match: obj25's key objective requires a goals-of-care plan that 'maintains human dignity' -- the explicit organizing principle behind this unit's palliative sedation therapy (reserved for refractory symptoms in the final hours, only after specialist consultation) and dignity therapy (structured life-review questions) content.

testable_competencies.refractory_symptoms: Recognize palliative sedation therapy as an option reserved for intolerable, refractory physical symptoms in the final hours of life, requiring specialist palliative care consultation.
testable_competencies.multidimensional_assessment: Identify the multidimensional (physical, social-relational, psychological, spiritual, existential) sources of suffering in a palliative patient, recognizing that suffering is subjective and not confined to physical symptoms.

entries.title: Medical Assistance in Dying (MAID)

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service; https://mcc.ca/objectives/medical-expert/dying-patients/, version March 2026)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Direct, explicit match: obj25's key objective states the candidate 'must know the provisions in Canadian law on medical assistance in dying (MAID), be prepared to discuss them with patients, and respond appropriately to such requests,' and its enabling objectives require 'providing a compassionate response to any request for MAID and taking appropriate steps to ensure the patient has access to this intervention if they meet the eligibility criteria (e.g., make a referral).'

testable_competencies.eligibility_pathways: Distinguish MAID Track 1 (natural death reasonably foreseeable) from Track 2 (serious and incurable illness/disease/disability, death not reasonably foreseeable) eligibility pathways.
testable_competencies.response_to_request: Respond to a patient's MAID request with a compassionate, non-judgmental approach and take appropriate steps toward referral if the patient meets eligibility criteria, recognizing the current mental-illness-sole-criterion exclusion.

entries.cross_discipline_note: MAID eligibility and process are also foundational to ELOM's end-of-life legal/ethical content; this unit is retained here (rather than exclusively in ELOM) because obj25 -- the chapter's primary Medical Expert anchor -- names MAID directly as part of the dying-patient clinical objective. PRIMARY_OWNER/CROSS_LINK/DISTINCT_CONTEXT designation is deferred to the global cross-chapter ownership audit per project instruction.

entries.title: Types of Grief (Anticipatory, Acute, Complicated)

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service; https://mcc.ca/objectives/medical-expert/dying-patients/, version March 2026)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Obj25's key objective requires recognizing 'the importance of family, social supports' in the goals-of-care plan, which frames bereavement/grief support, though the objective text does not itself define grief subtypes; this unit's specific anticipatory/acute/complicated-grief taxonomy is a narrower, more specific concept than the objective's general family-support language.

testable_competencies.grief_recognition: Distinguish normal anticipatory/acute grief from complicated grief (prolonged duration, maladaptive thoughts, dysregulated emotions, dysfunctional behaviours, with prevalent comorbid depression/anxiety) as a trigger for additional support or referral.

entries.cross_discipline_note: Distinguishing complicated grief from a major depressive episode has diagnostic overlap with Psychiatry; this unit's scope is recognition in the palliative/bereavement context rather than formal psychiatric diagnostic criteria.

mcc_evidence.objective_title: Professional - Accountability to physician health and well-being for provision of optimal patient care
mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (role-level record; no per-objective ID exists for this role)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Group's enabling text directly matches this unit: 'manage influences on personal well-being that may affect professional performance,' 'manage personal and professional demands to ensure sustainable practice,' and 'promote a culture that recognises, responds to, and supports colleagues in need.'

testable_competencies.provider_wellbeing: Recognize that provider self-care positively predicts compassion satisfaction and negatively predicts burnout/compassion fatigue, and identify workplace and personal self-care strategies.

entries.title: Pediatric Palliative Care: Unique Considerations and Patient Categories

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service; https://mcc.ca/objectives/medical-expert/dying-patients/, version March 2026)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Obj25's 'dying patient' framing is written generally rather than adult-specific, and its family/SDM/goals-of-care enabling objectives apply directly to the pediatric context described in this unit (family-centred decision-making tied to the child's developmental capacity); no separate pediatric-specific palliative-care MCC objective exists in the candidate set, so this general obj25 match is used with MODERATE rather than STRONG strength.

testable_competencies.pediatric_considerations: Recognize that the unit of pediatric palliative care is the family (including siblings), that decision-making authority tracks the child's developmental capacity rather than chronological age, and identify the four ACT/RCPCH categories of children who may benefit from palliative care.

entries.cross_discipline_note: Pediatric-specific EOL/palliative content also intersects the completed Pediatrics (P) chapter; PRIMARY_OWNER/CROSS_LINK designation across P and PM is deferred to the global cross-chapter ownership audit.

entries.title: Pediatric Palliative Care Assessment Tools (SSPedi, Mini-SSPedi, MSAS)

testable_competencies.instrument_awareness: Named pediatric symptom-screening instruments (SSPedi, Mini-SSPedi, MSAS) that frame the chapter but are not independently tested at generalist scope.

entries.zero_question_reason: Specific validated-instrument names and their exact age cutoffs/Likert-scale points are specialist-level detail with no dedicated MCC objective; not planned for dedicated question coverage at this scope stage, consistent with the OT audiometric-testing-instrument precedent.

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service; https://mcc.ca/objectives/medical-expert/dying-patients/, version March 2026)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Obj25's symptom-control and family-involvement enabling objectives extend to the pediatric context this unit covers (shared decision-making with the child and parents, developmentally-matched communication about diagnosis/prognosis, play therapy); no dedicated pediatric-palliative MCC objective exists, so MODERATE strength is used.

testable_competencies.pediatric_communication: Recognize that open, developmentally-matched communication with the child about diagnosis/prognosis reduces anxiety, and that shared decision-making with both child (to the extent possible) and parents guides pediatric EOL care.

entries.title: Equity in Palliative Care (Barriers to Access, Anti-Oppressive Care)

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service; https://mcc.ca/objectives/medical-expert/population-health-and-its-determinants/providing-anti-oppressive-health-care/, version March 2023)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Direct match confirmed by Study Smarter 2026's own discipline mapping (legacy_id 127 tagged to this chapter under the PHELO discipline): obj127's key objectives require providing inclusive care and recognizing effects of stigmatization/discrimination based on factors including race, disability, income, and sexual orientation -- precisely the barriers-to-access list (older age, race, homelessness, low socioeconomic status, disability, immigrant status, sexual/gender minority status) taught in this unit.

testable_competencies.equity_barriers: Identify patient/system characteristics associated with poorer access to palliative care (older age, race, unmarried/living alone, non-cancer diagnosis, sexual/gender minority status, homelessness, low socioeconomic status, long-term-care residence, rurality, disability, immigrant status) and the need to account for one's own biases in providing equitable palliative care.

entries.title: Landmark Palliative Medicine Trials (EBM Summary Table)

testable_competencies.evidence_awareness: EBM trial-summary reference table; not independently tested as a discrete competency at this scope stage.

entries.zero_question_reason: Reference/EBM-summary content (trial names, methods, and statistical results); not planned for dedicated question coverage at this scope stage, consistent with the project's reference-table treatment precedent.
